ModMetaData.name: Dyze Pathogenic Residue
ModMetaData.author: Dyze
ModMetaData.description:
[h1]Dyze's Pathogenics[/h1]
[b]Realistic disease spread for RimWorld colonies.[/b]
Dyze's Pathogenics adds a more realistic disease transmission system to RimWorld.
Instead of diseases appearing only as isolated random events, infections can enter the colony through outsiders such as visitors, traders, raiders, prisoners, refugees, and other temporary pawns.
Pawns may carry an illness before symptoms appear, spread it through close contact and shared air, and trigger colony-wide outbreaks if the infection is not contained.
[hr][/hr]
[h2]Current focus[/h2]
The first version focuses on a standalone respiratory disease prototype.
[list] [*]Outsider-based disease importation [*]Hidden incubation before visible symptoms [*]Pre-symptomatic infectious stage [*]Exposure accumulation instead of instant infection rolls [*]Proximity-based respiratory spread [*]Higher risk in shared indoor spaces [*]Debug tools for testing and balancing [/list]
[hr][/hr]
[h2]Design goal[/h2]
Dyze's Pathogenics aims to make disease feel less like a random medical event and more like a colony management problem.
Shared bedrooms, dining rooms, hospitals, prisons, visitors, and quarantine decisions should matter. A sick pawn is not just a patient. They are a possible outbreak source.
[hr][/hr]
[h2]Development status[/h2]
This mod is currently in active development.
The old floor-residue concept is being replaced by a cleaner disease simulation model focused on infection paths, incubation, exposure, and transmission behavior.
[h3]Planned direction[/h3]
[list] [*]Standalone simulated respiratory disease [*]More detailed outbreak behavior [*]Disease-specific transmission paths [*]Better player feedback [*]Optional future support for surface contamination, quarantine tools, and additional disease types [/list]
[hr][/hr]
[h2]Compatibility[/h2]
Dyze's Pathogenics is designed to avoid overwriting vanilla Defs where possible.
The goal is to build disease behavior through custom Defs, extensions, settings, and lightweight runtime systems rather than hardcoded changes to every disease.
[hr][/hr]
[h2]Safe removal[/h2]
As this mod is still evolving, removing it from an existing save is not recommended unless a safe removal path is explicitly provided for the version you are using.
